examples.en: That person's life was a thorny path.
After walking a thorny path, he finally succeeded.
The road of a new actor is a thorny one.
I got through a time that felt like a thorny path.
Everyone says starting a business is a thorny road.

examples.ko: 가시밭길에도 함께 가는 친구가 있어서 힘이 났어요.
examples.en: Even on a thorny path, I had a friend beside me and felt strong.

explain: 진짜 가시가 있는 길보다 힘들고 어려운 삶이나 과정을 비유할 때 훨씬 많이 써요. '가시밭길을 걷다'가 가장 자연스러운 짝이에요. 반대로 쉽고 편한 길은 '꽃길'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: He walked a thorny path for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 자연스러운 짝말로 힘든 삶을 비유해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural pairing, used figuratively for a hard life.

phrases.en: My mother's hard life came out as a movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어렵게 산 삶 전체를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a whole life of hardship.

phrases.en: May you walk only easy and happy paths from now on.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가시밭길'의 반대로, 행복하고 쉬운 앞날을 빌 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of '가시밭길', used to wish someone a happy future.

explain_en: It is used far more as a metaphor for a hard life or process than for a path with real thorns. '가시밭길을 걷다' is the most natural pairing. The opposite, an easy and happy road, is '꽃길'.

en: to be winding; to be crooked

examples.ko: 이 길은 너무 꾸불꾸불해서 멀미가 나요.
examples.en: This road is so winding that I get carsick.
I passed through the winding alleys and arrived at the market.
The handwriting is so squiggly that it's hard to read.
The way the river winds along is beautiful.
My hair is wavy, so I straighten it every morning.
The mountain road is winding, so drive carefully.

explain: 주로 길, 강 같은 큰 것이 여러 번 휘어 있을 때 쓰고, 멀미가 나거나 운전 조심하라는 말과 자주 이어져요. 글씨나 머리카락이 고르지 않게 휘었을 때도 써요. 작고 가는 것에는 '꼬불꼬불하다'가 더 어울려요.

phrases.en: We walked along the winding river.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ'을 붙여 길, 강처럼 크게 휘는 것을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -ㄴ it describes big curving things like roads and rivers.

phrases.example: 이 길은 꾸불꾸불하지 않아서 운전하기 편해요.
phrases.en: This road isn't winding, so it's easy to drive.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길이 곧다는 걸 부정형으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says the road is fairly straight.

phrases.en: The alley was twisty, so I got lost.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 작고 가는 것이 휠 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for smaller, finer things that twist.

explain_en: It is mainly used for big things like roads and rivers with many bends, and often goes with remarks about carsickness or careful driving. It also describes uneven, wavy handwriting or hair. For small, thin things, '꼬불꼬불하다' fits better.

examples.en: An old shipwreck was found at the bottom of the sea.
Divers are examining the wreck.
Lots of old ceramics were recovered from the wreck.
In the movie, the main character gets trapped in a wrecked ship.
Debris from the wreck washed up onto the beach.

examples.ko: 그 낡은 배는 마치 난파선 같아요.
examples.en: That old boat looks just like a shipwreck.

explain: 부서지거나 가라앉은 배 자체를 말해요. 낡고 망가진 배를 보고 '난파선 같다'고 비유해서 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: The research team examined the wreck on the seabed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가라앉은 배를 살펴볼 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used when examining a sunken ship.

phrases.en: An old wreck was discovered.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 자주 쓰는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A passive expression often used in the news.

phrases.example: 이 낡은 배는 꼭 난파선 같아요.
phrases.en: This old boat looks just like a wreck.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낡고 망가진 것을 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively for something old and broken.

explain_en: It refers to the broken or sunken ship itself. People also use it figuratively, saying an old, battered boat is 'like a wreck' ('난파선 같다').

examples.en: I took a trip to the west coast over the weekend.
The sunset seen from the west coast is really pretty.
On the west coast the tide comes in and out a lot.
The west coast highway was jammed, so I was late.
They say it will rain a lot on the west coast.
I dug for clams on the west coast mudflats.

explain: 한국에서는 서쪽 바다, 곧 황해를 따라 있는 바닷가를 말해요. 동해안과 달리 갯벌이 넓고 물이 빠졌다 들어오는 차이가 커요. 반대쪽은 '동해안', 남쪽은 '남해안'이에요.

phrases.en: If you take the West Coast Expressway, you'll arrive quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서해안을 따라 남북으로 이어진 고속도로 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name of the expressway that runs north-south along the west coast.

phrases.en: There are many tidal flats in the west coast area.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서해안 근처의 넓은 지역을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the wider area near the west coast.

phrases.en: I watched the sun set over the West Sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: '서해안'은 바닷가이고 '서해'는 바다 자체를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '서해안' is the shore, while '서해' is the sea itself.

explain_en: In Korea it refers to the coast along the western sea, the Yellow Sea. Unlike the east coast, it has wide mudflats and a big tidal range. The other coasts are 동해안 (east) and 남해안 (south).

examples.ko: 긴 항해를 마치고 배가 항구에 도착했어요.
examples.en: After the long voyage, the ship arrived at the port.
A voyage is safe only when the weather is good.

examples.ko: 이 배는 내일 아침에 항해에 나서요.
examples.en: This ship sets out on a voyage tomorrow morning.
The captain has long experience at sea.
It was my first voyage, so I was a little scared.

examples.ko: 세계 일주 항해 이야기를 책으로 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read the story of a voyage around the world in a book.

explain: '항해'는 배가 바다를 건너 다니는 일이고, 비행기가 하늘을 나는 일은 '비행'이라고 해요. 여행으로 배를 타는 것은 '배 여행'이나 '크루즈'라고 하는 편이 자연스러워요. '항해'는 이야기나 역사, 모험에 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The ship set off on a long voyage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배가 바다로 나가기 시작할 때 쓰는 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pair for a ship starting out to sea.
phrases.en_equiv: to set out on a voyage

phrases.en: The ship is sailing right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 바다를 가고 있는 상태를 짧게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short way to say it is currently at sea.

phrases.en: This ship's first voyage was a success.
phrases.nuance_ko: 처음으로 바다를 건너는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the first time a ship goes out to sea.

explain_en: 항해 is a ship traveling across the sea, and a plane flying through the sky is 비행. For a leisure trip on a ship, 배 여행 or 크루즈 sounds more natural. 항해 appears often in stories, history and adventures.

examples.en: Independence activists suffered in prison during the Japanese colonial period.

examples.ko: 서대문 형무소가 지금은 역사 박물관이 됐어요.
examples.en: Seodaemun Prison has now become a history museum.
In the old days, a correctional facility was called a hyeongmuso.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 형무소에 갇혔던 이야기를 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandfather told me about the time he was locked up in prison.

examples.ko: 영화 속 주인공이 형무소를 탈출하는 장면이 인상적이었어요.
examples.en: The scene where the hero escapes from prison in the movie was impressive.
That prison closed down a long time ago.

explain: 지금은 '교도소'라고 하고, '형무소'는 일제강점기나 옛날 이야기, 역사 수업에서 주로 나와요. 현대의 감옥을 가리킬 때 쓰면 어색해요.

phrases.en: He was locked up in prison and suffered for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛날 이야기에서 감옥에 들어가 있었다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in historical contexts to mean being held in prison.
phrases.en_equiv: to be locked up in prison

phrases.en: I went to Seodaemun Prison and learned about history.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이름이 그대로 남은 역사적인 장소를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a historic place whose name has remained.

phrases.en: These days it is called a correctional facility.
phrases.nuance_ko: 현대에 쓰는 말이에요. 지금의 감옥은 '교도소'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modern word; today's prisons are called 교도소.

explain_en: Today the standard word is '교도소'; '형무소' mainly appears in talk about the Japanese colonial period, old times and history lessons. Using it for a modern prison sounds odd.

examples.ko: 이 다리는 강철로 만들어서 아주 튼튼해요.
examples.en: This bridge is made of steel, so it is very sturdy.
Steel is much harder than ordinary iron.

examples.ko: 이 가위는 강철이라서 오래 써도 잘 안 닳아요.
examples.en: These scissors are made of steel, so they hardly wear out even with long use.
They are putting up steel pillars at the construction site.
Steel supports the frame of the building.
My father works at a factory that makes steel.

explain: 일상에서는 '철'이나 '쇠'를 더 자주 말하고, '강철'은 철보다 훨씬 튼튼하다는 점을 말할 때 써요. '철'은 금속 이름이고 '쇠'는 말할 때 금속 전체를 가리키는 느낌이에요. 건물, 다리, 기계 이야기에 나와요.

phrases.example: 그 선수는 강철 같은 체력으로 끝까지 뛰었어요.
phrases.en: be like steel
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이나 마음이 아주 단단하고 쉽게 꺾이지 않는다는 뜻이에요. 보통 '강철 같은 의지', '강철 같은 체력'처럼 명사 앞에서 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes a body or mind that is very tough and does not break easily. It usually comes before a noun, as in '강철 같은 의지' or '강철 같은 체력'.

explain_en: In daily speech 철 or 쇠 is used more often; 강철 is for stressing that something is much tougher than plain iron. 철 is the name of the metal, while 쇠 is the spoken word that feels like metal in general. It comes up in talk about buildings, bridges, and machines.

examples.en: There are many stone walls on Jeju Island.

examples.ko: 마을 가옥들은 대부분 돌담으로 둘러싸여 있어요.
examples.en: Most houses in the village are surrounded by stone walls.
A cat is walking along the top of the stone wall.
Little flowers have bloomed at the foot of the stone wall.
I can see the neighbor's yard over the stone wall.
It's a low stone wall, so it's easy to climb over.

explain: 돌을 쌓아서 만든 담이에요. 흙담이나 시멘트 담과 재료가 달라요. 제주도나 시골 마을의 옛 풍경을 말할 때 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I walked slowly along the stone-wall path.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돌담이 이어진 길을 말하고 분위기 있는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A lane lined with stone walls, with a scenic feel.

phrases.en: The villagers built a stone wall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 담을 만드는 동작은 '쌓다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 'Ssata' (to pile up) is the verb for building such a wall.

phrases.en: I can see a persimmon tree over the stone wall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 담 뒤쪽을 말할 때 '너머'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '너머' to mean the far side of the wall.

explain_en: It is a wall built by stacking stones, different in material from an earth wall or a cement wall. It often appears when describing old scenery on Jeju Island or in country villages.

examples.ko: 마당에 멍석을 깔고 고추를 널어 말렸어요.
examples.en: We spread a straw mat in the yard and dried red peppers on it.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 멍석 위에서 수박을 먹었던 기억이 나요.
examples.en: I remember eating watermelon on a straw mat as a child.

examples.ko: 마을 사람들이 멍석에 둘러앉아 이야기를 나눴어요.
examples.en: The villagers sat around a straw mat and talked.

examples.ko: 비가 오자 할머니가 멍석을 급히 걷으셨어요.
examples.en: When it started to rain, my grandmother quickly took in the straw mat.

examples.ko: 팀장님이 멍석을 깔아 주셔서 제 생각을 마음껏 말했어요.
examples.en: My team leader gave me the stage, so I could say what I thought freely.

examples.ko: 시골 장터 한쪽에 멍석을 펴고 나물을 파는 할머니가 계셨어요.
examples.en: At one side of the country market, an old woman sat selling wild greens on a spread straw mat.

explain: 짚으로 엮어 마당에 깔고 곡식을 말리는 큰 자리예요. 요즘은 실물보다 '멍석을 깔다'라는 관용 표현으로도 쓰여요. 비슷한 '돗자리'는 놀러 갈 때 까는 자리로, 쓰임이 달라요.

phrases.example: 친구들이 멍석을 깔아 줘서 신나게 노래했어요.
phrases.en: My friends set the stage for me, so I sang happily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하고 싶은 일을 마음껏 할 수 있는 자리를 만들어 준다는 느낌으로 써요. '멍석을 깔아 주다'처럼 말할 때가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means creating a space where someone can freely do what they want. It is often said as '멍석을 깔아 주다'.
phrases.en_equiv: give someone the floor / set the stage for someone

explain_en: It is a large mat woven from straw, spread in a yard to dry grain. Today it also appears in the idiom '멍석을 깔다' rather than only as a real object. A similar word, '돗자리', is a mat for picnics, so the use is different.

examples.ko: 할머니 댁 마당에 지푸라기가 여기저기 널려 있어요.
examples.en: Straw is scattered all over the yard at my grandmother's house.
You have straw stuck on your clothes. Didn't you notice?
In the old days, people made shoes out of straw and wore them.

examples.ko: 아기 돼지 이야기에서 첫째는 지푸라기로 집을 지어요.
examples.en: In the story of the three little pigs, the first one builds a house of straw.
I wove straw together and made a small basket.

examples.ko: 바닥에 지푸라기 하나 안 남기고 깨끗이 치웠어요.
examples.en: I cleaned up so well that not a single piece of straw was left on the floor.

explain: 짚 한 가닥이나 부스러기처럼 작고 가벼운 것을 가리켜서 '지푸라기 하나'처럼 하나씩 셀 때도 많아요. 비유로 쓰일 때는 힘없고 약한 것을 말하는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.example: 너무 급해서 물에 빠지면 지푸라기라도 잡는다고 아무 방법이나 써 봤어요.
phrases.en: I was so desperate that I tried any method at all, like a drowning person clutching at straws.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 급하고 절박하면 도움이 안 될 것 같은 것에도 매달린다는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning that when people are desperate, they cling even to things that probably won't help.

explain_en: It often points to small, light bits of straw, so people count it like '지푸라기 하나' (a single piece of straw). In figurative use it carries a feeling of something weak and fragile.

examples.ko: 집 앞에 있는 철문이 너무 무거워요.
examples.en: The iron gate in front of my house is too heavy.
This iron door only opens with a key.
I waited for my friend in front of the school's iron gate.
Please make sure to lock the iron gate at night.
If you go in through the iron door in the back alley, you'll find the shop.
Please don't lock your bike to the iron gate.

explain: '대문'은 집의 큰 문이고 '철문'은 쇠로 만든 문이라서, 쇠로 만든 대문을 철문이라고 부를 수 있어요. 무겁고 단단하고 차가운 느낌이 있어서 소리나 무게 이야기와 같이 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The caretaker opens the iron gate every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무거운 문을 연다는 기본 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic verb pairing for opening the gate.

phrases.en: I always lock the iron gate at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문단속을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when talking about locking up.

phrases.en: The heavy iron door slammed shut.
phrases.nuance_ko: 철문의 무겁고 단단한 느낌을 꾸며 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Emphasizes the heavy, solid feel of the door.

explain_en: '대문' is a house's main gate, while '철문' describes a door made of iron, so an iron main gate can be called a 철문. It feels heavy, hard and cold, so it often comes up with talk of sound or weight.

en: to plead; to request earnestly; to beg

examples.ko: 아이가 강아지를 키우게 해 달라고 간청했어요.
examples.en: The child begged to be allowed to raise a puppy.

examples.ko: 친구가 도와 달라고 간청해서 거절하지 못했어요.
examples.en: My friend begged me for help, so I couldn't refuse.

examples.ko: 그는 눈물을 흘리며 한 번만 용서해 달라고 간청해요.
examples.en: He begs with tears to be forgiven just once.

examples.ko: 여러 번 간청하는데도 선생님은 허락하지 않으셨어요.
examples.en: Even though I pleaded many times, the teacher didn't allow it.

examples.ko: 부모님께 유학을 보내 달라고 간청하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to beg my parents to let me study abroad.
You don't have to beg. I'll help you first.

explain: '부탁하다'보다 훨씬 절실하게 매달리는 느낌이에요. '간청을 들어주다', '간청을 거절하다', '간청에 못 이겨'처럼 명사 '간청'으로도 자주 써요. 비슷한 말로는 '애원하다', '사정하다'가 있어요.

phrases.en: The teacher granted the student's plea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '간청'을 써서 부탁을 받아 주는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun '간청' for accepting an earnest request.

phrases.example: 그는 한 번만 용서해 달라고 애원했어요.
phrases.en: He begged to be forgiven just once.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말이고 더 눈물겹게 매달리는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word with a more desperate, tearful feel.

phrases.example: 아이의 간청에 못 이겨 강아지를 샀어요.
phrases.en: I gave in to my child's pleading and bought a puppy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계속된 부탁 때문에 결국 허락했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means one finally agreed because of repeated pleading.

explain_en: It feels much more desperate and pleading than '부탁하다' (to ask). The noun '간청' is also common, as in '간청을 들어주다' (grant a plea), '간청을 거절하다' and '간청에 못 이겨' (unable to resist the plea). Similar words are '애원하다' and '사정하다'.

examples.ko: 시험 결과가 나오기 전에는 경거망동하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't act rashly before the exam results come out.
I still regret getting excited and acting rashly.

examples.ko: 이럴 때일수록 경거망동하지 말고 신중하게 행동해요.
examples.en: At times like this, don't act rashly; be careful.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 늘 경거망동해서 주변에서 걱정해요.
examples.en: He always acts rashly, so the people around him worry.

examples.ko: 처음 만난 자리에서 경거망동했다가 큰 실수를 했어요.
examples.en: I behaved rashly at our first meeting and made a big mistake.

examples.ko: 아이들이 경거망동할까 봐 미리 주의를 줬어요.
examples.en: I warned the kids in advance in case they behaved recklessly.

explain: 대부분 '-지 마세요', '-면 안 돼요'처럼 금지나 경고와 함께 써요. '까불다, 함부로 행동하다'와 비슷하지만 더 딱딱하고 무게가 있는 말이에요.

phrases.en: Please don't act rashly right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정중하게 경고하거나 당부할 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common polite way to warn or urge someone.

phrases.en: I was angry and acted rashly. I'm sorry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 한 가벼운 행동을 반성하며 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when reflecting on a rash thing already done.

phrases.en: Don't behave carelessly in a place you don't know.
phrases.nuance_ko: '경거망동하다'보다 쉽고 일상적인 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, more everyday near-synonym of '경거망동하다'.

explain_en: It is mostly used with prohibitions or warnings, like '-지 마세요' or '-면 안 돼요'. It is similar to '까불다' or '함부로 행동하다' but sounds stiffer and heavier.

examples.en: My father brings the axe down hard on the firewood.

examples.ko: 그 선수가 공을 상대 코트로 세게 내리찍었어요.
examples.en: That player slammed the ball down into the opponent's court.
It is dangerous to use a knife by chopping down like that.
Be careful of your hand when you bring the hammer down.

examples.ko: 얼음을 깨려고 곡괭이로 내리찍는 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: I can hear someone hacking down with a pickaxe to break the ice.
If you stamp down hard on the seal, the letters smear.

explain: 그냥 '찍다'와 달리 위에서 아래로 힘을 실어 내려칠 때 써요. 도끼, 망치, 곡괭이처럼 무게가 있는 도구와 잘 어울려요. 사진을 찍는 뜻은 없어요.

phrases.en: Grandfather chopped the log with an axe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무거운 도구를 위에서 아래로 쓸 때 가장 잘 어울리는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The best-fitting pairing for using a heavy tool from above to below.

phrases.en: The worker struck the hard ground with a pickaxe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곡괭이처럼 끝이 뾰족한 도구로 힘을 실어 세게 찍을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when striking hard with a pointed tool like a pickaxe.
phrases.en_equiv: to strike down with a pickaxe

phrases.en: The player smashed the ball down into the opponent's court.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형이에요. 스포츠에서 공을 위에서 세게 내리칠 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form. Also used in sports when hitting a ball down hard.

explain_en: Unlike plain '찍다', this means bringing something down from above with force. It pairs well with heavy tools such as axes, hammers and pickaxes. It never means taking a photo.

en: to fight; to compete; to match

examples.en: The small team took on the title favorite.
It's hard to take on ten people alone.
There is no player who can match him.

examples.ko: 우리는 강한 상대와 대적해 볼 생각이에요.
examples.en: We plan to try going up against a strong opponent.

examples.ko: 대적하는 두 나라의 관계가 점점 나빠졌어요.
examples.en: The relationship between the two opposing countries got worse and worse.

examples.ko: 큰 회사에 대적하려면 좋은 아이디어가 필요해요.
examples.en: To go up against a big company, you need good ideas.

explain: 힘이 비슷하거나 더 센 상대와 맞서 겨룰 때 써요. 보통 '~와/과 대적하다' 꼴이고, '대적할 사람이 없다', '대적할 수 없다'처럼 부정문에서 특히 많이 나와요. 일상에서는 '맞서다'가 더 편하게 들려요.

phrases.example: 그 선수는 너무 강해서 아무도 대적할 수 없어요.
phrases.en: That player is so strong that no one can match him.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대가 너무 강하다는 뜻으로 부정문에서 특히 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Especially common in the negative to say an opponent is too strong.

phrases.example: 우리 팀이 이번에 강팀과 대적하게 됐어요.
phrases.en: Our team ended up facing a strong team this time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~와/과' 뒤에 겨루는 상대가 와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opponent you compete against comes before '와/과'.

phrases.en: The small team stood up to the big team.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대적하다'와 비슷하지만 일상 대화에서 더 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close to '대적하다' but sounds more casual in daily speech.

explain_en: Use it when standing against and competing with an opponent of equal or greater strength. It usually takes the form '~와/과 대적하다', and it appears especially often in negatives such as '대적할 사람이 없다' or '대적할 수 없다'. In daily talk '맞서다' sounds more natural.

gh: general fight or argue; everyday word
struggle for a cause or rights
face off in a match; formal

p.n: The original means standing up to a rival; the replacement is a colloquial direct clash.
